goal.title: Calculate prices with sequential changes
goal.questionDirective: Give two different practical price problems combining a percentage change with a fixed charge. State the order and every amount explicitly. Ask for an exact final price or original price.

goal.title: Predict Python dictionary updates
goal.questionDirective: Give two different short executable Python 3 snippets using dictionary get or setdefault with mutable lists. Include all initialization and print calls. Test the resulting dictionary after a retrieved list changes.

goal.title: Interpret deductions about past events in English
goal.questionDirective: Give two short situations and ask which sentence expresses the stated level of certainty about a past event. Make time and certainty matter; do not ask merely which sentence is grammatical.

sourceDocuments.name: Study notes
sourceDocuments.text: For these practice questions, must have + past participle expresses a strong positive deduction about a past event. Might have + past participle expresses a possibility, without a strong conclusion. Cannot have + past participle expresses a strong negative deduction about a past event. Should have + past participle can express criticism or regret about an action that would have been preferable. These expressions describe the speaker’s judgment; they are not mathematical proof that the event did or did not happen.

goal.title: Learn the fictional Alder reserve handbook
goal.questionDirective: Ask two questions that combine an animal’s area with that area’s keeper. Test recall and application of the handbook without restating the tested facts.

sourceDocuments.name: Alder reserve handbook
sourceDocuments.text: This fictional reserve has exactly four animal areas. Grove houses only foxes; Lake houses only otters; Cliff houses only falcons; Meadow houses only deer. Marta alone manages Grove, Niko alone manages Lake, Ola alone manages Cliff, and Paz alone manages Meadow. Each animal type occurs in its named area only.
